title: Covered in scales
hook: A covering can protect without being armor made of metal.

knows: Animals have body structures and life histories.
doesNotKnow: Identify pangolin scales as a protective covering.

misconception: A familiar animal feature always has the first explanation that comes to mind.
objective: Identify pangolin scales as a protective covering.

claims.text: When a pangolin rolls up, what forms the protective outer surface? The schematic shows a curled body with overlapping scales on the outside. Pangolin scales are part of the animal’s body; curling presents the scaled surface outward. The drawing simplifies their shape and arrangement.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: Smithsonian National Zoo, pangolin, https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/pangolin

claims.text: The diagram and its labels are schematic, not to scale and not an observation. Protective covering · schematic
When a pangolin curls, why can this posture help protect its softer underside? Pangolins have scales that form a protective covering when curled.
